newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 2.

text.p: Fuji Co Ltd, a medium-sized supermarket operator listed on the over-the-counter market, is considering issuing convertible bonds within this week, following the deregulation started in January. Nomura Securities Co Ltd is expected to be a lead manager.
Onward Kashiyama Co Ltd is expected to have increased its parent current profit to more than 7.3 billion yen in the first half ended August 31, up 17 percent from the same period a year earlier.

Kao Corp plans to join Planet Inc's product information and distribution network, which was launched in 1985 by twelve leading household product makers such as Lion Corp and Uni-Charm Corp. More than 90 companies, mainly household product makers, currently form Planet's network.

Oki Electric Industry Co Ltd has decided to postpone its semiconductor plant construction project planned for this year, due to weak sales in the chip market. Oki also plans to cut capital investment in the semiconductor division by about three billion yen.

Honda Motor Co Ltd and Nissan Motor Co Ltd are planning to boost vehicle production in Britain as early as 1998. Honda targets annual production of 30,000 units, rising to 150,000 units in 1998. Nissan also hopes to manufacture 20,000 units annually.

Toray Industries Inc plans to triple annual production capacity of polyester film to about 90,000 tonnes over the next seven years at its subsidiary in France. Total investment will be around 30 billion yen. It hopes to boost its share of the film market in Europe for magnetic materials applications from the current 20 percent to more than 30 percent.

Mitsui Home Co Ltd is to expand its home renovation business by increasing the number of franchised subcontractors, in cooperation with its interior design unit Mitsui Designtek Co Ltd. It hopes to increase its orders to 50 billion yen annually in the business year starting April 1, 2000.

Nisshin Flour Milling Co Ltd plans to set up a plant worth 3.1 billion yen by the spring of 1998 to produce and sell pasta in the United States. It may export the products back to Japan. The new company, capitalised at $4 million, is expected to start operations from the spring of 1998.
